messages:
rachel: Hi all! First day. I finished Okta SSO & installed the VPN client but can't reach bastion.redwood.internal or our docker registry. VPN shows connected. Any quick tips?

devops-bot: Welcome @rachel! Tagging @morgan (IT) and @netops. Onboarding doc: https://internal.redwood/onboarding/vpn-access

morgan: Hi Rachel  are you on BYOD or company laptop? Which OS and VPN client/version?

rachel: BYOD MacBook Pro, macOS 14.5, client SecureEdge 6.0.1 via SSO.

netops: Most likely split-tunnel not getting pushed. Can you run `netstat -rn | grep 10.` and `scutil --dns` and paste outputs? Also check client shows "split tunnel" or "full tunnel".

rachel: `netstat` shows no 10.* routes. `scutil --dns` only lists my home DNS. Client UI says split-tunnel enabled.

morgan: Ok. Quick test: enable "Route all traffic" in the client to see if you can reach things (temporary). If that fails, we can open a short firewall rule to bastion and use jump host.

rachel: Toggled route-all, reconnected -> still can't resolve bastion. `dig bastion.redwood.internal` -> NXDOMAIN.

netops: Please run `dig bastion.redwood.internal @10.40.0.10` (our internal DNS). If that times out the DNS push didn't apply. Also what's the client profile id? You can grab it from the client logs (Preferences > Help > Export logs).

rachel: `dig` to 10.40.0.10 times out. I exported logs but it's a big bundle. Where should I upload?

morgan: Upload logs to the onboarding ticket (ONB-6001) or attach to a DM to me. Meanwhile I'll open a 30m firewall exception for your IP so you can use the public jump host.

netops: I've pushed a temporary policy to include 10.40.0.0/16 and DNS 10.40.0.10 for the `onboard-2027` profile family. Restart the client in ~2m. If your client hides profile id, that's fine; the family push should cover 6.0.x.

rachel: Restarted client -> still no 10.* routes. `netstat` unchanged.

morgan: Hm, some SecureEdge builds ignore pushed routes until the profile fingerprint matches. Can you paste the client build ID from the Help > About screen?

rachel: Build ID SE-6.0.1-rc2.

netops: That explains it  rc builds require explicit profile id push. I've added your build to the push list and forced a policy refresh. Please reconnect.

rachel: Reconnected -> now `netstat -rn | grep 10.` shows routes, `dig bastion.redwood.internal @10.40.0.10` returns 10.40.2.7. SSH to bastion works.

rachel: Docker pull still stalls at TLS handshake. `curl -v https://registry.redwood.internal:5000/v2/` shows cert CN=registry.internal (name mismatch).

morgan: That's a cert SAN issue we still see occasionally. Workarounds: 1) use registry IP `https://10.40.3.9:5000` temporarily, 2) we'll request a short-lived SAN add for `registry.redwood.internal` (ONB-6002). Netops, can you also check MTU issues?

netops: Sure. In many cases reducing tunnel MTU to 1400 fixes TLS hangs on mac tun stacks. Try `sudo ifconfig utun0 mtu 1400` and retry curl.

rachel: Lowering MTU -> curl now responds with 401 (auth) so TLS handshake completed. Docker pull works after I login. Everything seems fine now. Thanks!

morgan: Great. Follow-up: we'll add you to VPN-Onboarded Okta group so profile persists. We'll also update onboarding steps to ask for client build ID, `netstat` output, and public IP upfront for BYOD. Company laptop still recommended to avoid edge cases.

rachel: Thanks team, appreciate the fast help :tada:
